title: Angles of a Triangle
summary: Given a positive integer array of three elements, decide if a triangle with positive area can be formed.
statement: Given a positive integer array of three elements, decide if a triangle with positive area can be formed. If possible, return the angles of the triangle in non-decreasing order as floating-point numbers. If not, return an empty array. Acceptable answers are within 10^-5 of the correct values.
constraints: sides contains exactly three positive integers.
Return an empty list when the triangle inequality fails.
Otherwise return the three interior angles in nondecreasing degree order.
reference_solution:
def triangle_angles(sides):
    from math import acos,degrees
    a,b,c=sorted(sides)
    if a+b<=c:return []
    first=degrees(acos((b*b+c*c-a*a)/(2*b*c)))
    second=degrees(acos((a*a+c*c-b*b)/(2*a*c)))
    return [first,second,180-first-second]

def triangle_angles(sides):
    from math import acos,degrees
    a,b,c=sorted(sides)
    if a+b<=c:return []
    first=degrees(acos((b*b+c*c-a*a)/(2*b*c)))
    second=degrees(acos((a*a+c*c-b*b)/(2*a*c)))
    return [first,second,180-first+second]
hints: Sort the sides so both validity and angle order align.
Reject when the two smaller sides do not exceed the largest.
Apply the law of cosines to the first two angles and derive the third from their 180-degree sum.
Larger sides face larger angles, so sorted sides yield sorted results; the cosine law uniquely determines the valid triangle.
